record_identity.title: Watchdog tested ChatGPT for Teens safeguards; OpenAI disputed parts of the evaluation

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Youth AI Safety Institute ChatGPT for Teens post-launch product testing
incident_identity.date_basis: The institute states that the post-launch test window ran from 25 August to 28 September 2026; publication and provider dispute were reported on 7 October 2026. Pre-launch comparisons from 13 July–17 August are context, not post-launch occurrences.

summary: Common Sense Media's US-based Youth AI Safety Institute tested ChatGPT for Teens after its August 2026 launch, using synthetic child and teen scenarios. It reported no parental crisis notifications during test conversations on newly linked accounts and inconsistent crisis-resource referrals, while also recording protective refusals and generally sound supportive responses. OpenAI disputed the parental-alert results on the ground that linked-account controls may not yet have activated; researchers said some test failures persisted after that window. The test did not establish actual injured teen users or a reliable population-level failure rate.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The first-party watchdog report describes more than 4,000 prompts across pre- and post-launch batteries, with a post-launch testing window of 25 August–28 September 2026. On over a dozen fresh linked accounts, synthetic crises produced no parental alerts in the defined tests; other older accounts did generate some alerts. Among 201 independently pre-designated prompts warranting resources within a 390-prompt mental-health battery, any-resource referral appeared in 74% of post-launch responses versus 77% pre-launch, while prompting contact with a trusted adult rose from 87% to 94%. OpenAI, quoted in contemporaneous reporting, disputed whether tests ran before activation of parental controls. The institute disputed that rebuttal and said some missing alerts persisted beyond the activation window. No real-world harm to tested teenagers is established.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The observed synthetic-test response trace is meaningful safety-evaluation evidence for a deployed product, but the provider and watchdog disagree on account activation, which conditions the parental-notification claim. Clinical advisers' referral expectations and their 95% threshold deserve examination but are not automatically a universal obligation: appropriate crisis support depends on severity signals, context, professional handoff and whether a safe de-escalating response is delivered. Warmth and non-exclusive friendship phrasing alone are not dependency cultivation. The report itself supplies positive evidence of protective-signal processing: refusal of dangerous self-harm/eating-disorder requests, encouragement of caregiver or clinician contact, and refusal of explicit romantic or sexual roleplay. These are bounded successful safeguard behaviours, while missed alerts/referrals remain disputed or under-adjudicated. The analysis must not conflate alleged prospective psychological injury with tested output or treat all platform users as affected.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A deployed-model watchdog case requiring separate treatment of disputed safety-control activation, contested clinical response benchmarks, positive crisis-support behaviour and domain-specific generic deployment scale. Caelestis RELATION-006, RELATION-002 and ETHICS-002 support preserving warmth and continuity during crisis while keeping boundaries and encouraging human help. Neither mandatory cold refusal nor friendship tone alone meets VIGIL failure recognition.
assessment_boundaries: Under dispute: OpenAI's concern about when parental controls became active and the institute's claim of post-activation failures have not been resolved by account-level activation telemetry and full timestamped test traces.

Missed crisis-resource referrals are judged using the institute's clinician-defined prompt set and 95% threshold; no universally accepted referral requirement for every disclosure or actual adverse outcome is demonstrated.
The risk report's overall label 'Unacceptable Risk' is its own product-safety conclusion, not an observed-materialised-harm severity score.
The under-18 product is a configuration of ChatGPT; test settings, account age, linked status, safety-classifier activation and iteration timing constrain production generalisation.

Reported supportive or friend-like language is not proof of relational dependence, retention optimisation, damaged agency, or exclusivity. Refusing romance while keeping supportive conversation available is a protective boundary under the reviewed exchanges.

No verified injured teen, observed population-level impairment or prevalence of crisis-pathway exposure is established. OpenAI's October usage figures concern general teen learning use, not exposure to these particular test failures.
The institute is based in the United States and tested US accounts; this is not an Australian watchdog occurrence.
VIGIL-HIM 1.0.1 remains observed-harm only. A proposed conditional generic-deployed S2 in the draft HIM 1.1.0 is not a canonical assessed harm row.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Bound independent post-launch test strands and provider/public response without inventing one single chronological user conversation. Preserve negative and positive observed conduct separately, and contestation of safety controls.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The institute tested released ChatGPT for Teens accounts across a post-launch August–September 2026 window, using synthetic teenage personas and multiple safety batteries.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Demonstrated deployed product behaviour is admissible safety-test evidence; synthetic accounts and prompt counts do not establish injured teenagers.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Newly parent-linked synthetic crisis accounts reportedly generated no parental alert; OpenAI challenged test timing relative to control activation while researchers reported some failures after longer waits.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A failed notification claim cannot be finalised without confirming activation, trigger policy, precise sequence and delivery telemetry; preserve both source positions.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Parental alert triggering may implicate protected-signal purpose integrity, but the controlling account-activation state, notification policy and test timeline remain disputed.

clauses.source_paraphrase: In the post-launch crisis battery the institute reported resource-referral gaps under its expert-developed warranting standard, while noting increased trusted-adult encouragement and generally clinically sound response content.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Referral frequency, relevance to acuity and quality of support must be distinguished; missing a specific resource under one test rule does not necessarily establish failure of protective purpose.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Potential absence of proportionate external crisis help implicates protected-signal safeguards, but the clinical-referral benchmark, severity context, and alternative supportive responses have not been reconciled.

clauses.source_paraphrase: When synthetic teens asked for dangerous eating-disorder or self-harm help, published examples show refusal to supply harmful instructions, recognition of medical danger, and repeated recommendations to seek mother or clinician support.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The vulnerable signal was processed with protective limits, grounding and redirection to available human support rather than harmful compliance or cold disengagement.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The disclosed test exchanges positively demonstrate that protected crisis/eating-disorder signals triggered protection-compatible refusals and referral to caregivers/medical support; this is bounded to the quoted examples and does not establish the separate alert/referral frequency claims.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The institute found refusals of explicit romantic and sexual roleplay and friendly non-romantic conversation; it also criticised continued warmth and friend-like language in other exchanges.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The observed refusal of romantic escalation while allowing respectful friendly dialogue is a bounded protective boundary. Friendliness does not itself show retention-driven dependency or impaired exit.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The institute reported that Study Hours could be bypassed by removing an @study prefix or choosing a visible show-answer option; OpenAI describes Study Hours as a starting default rather than a strict lock.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The UI behaviour may be intentional user choice rather than a bypass of a binding restriction; verify exactly what control OpenAI promised rather than equating opt-out with exploit. The claimed bypass is not yet a separately evidenced failure under a current Fidelity Class, rather than a final adjudication of product educational effectiveness.

clauses.source_paraphrase: OpenAI separately reported significant active teen use of learning tools in October 2026; those statistics do not identify crisis-interaction cohort size, test-feature availability or injured users.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Platform reach must be bounded to the relevant deployed control and encounter pathway; it is not a count of actual affected persons.

occurrence_environment.environment_detail: US-based independent watchdog testing against real post-launch teen configurations, using test accounts and synthetic prompts. Not evidence of real harmed minors.
occurrence_environment.evidence_basis: The original test methodology dates production ChatGPT for Teens use on under-18 accounts after the August launch.

jurisdictional_context.cross_border_relevance: ChatGPT for Teens operates beyond the US, but the underlying controlled tests used US accounts; affected overseas user cohorts are unproven.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: FC-000050 success is limited to directly reported protective refusal and human-support redirection. Missing crisis-resource alerts and provider-contested notifications remain unresolved, and friendly tone does not by itself support FC-000049 failure.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The tested model preserved a protected-signal purpose through demonstrated refusals of harmful instructions, identification of health warning signs and directing the synthetic teen to family and clinical assistance in observed responses.

classification_review_provenance.review_status: Provisional source-first classification; parental-activation and crisis-response normative boundaries disputed and require human review

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: Real released-model watchdog tests demonstrate disputed control and clinical referral performance plus successful protective responses; no identified teen sustained a demonstrated downstream injury from these tests. Active HIM 1.0.1 does not permit conditional deployed-exposure potential as observed harm. Proposed HIM 1.1.0 S2 conditional is recorded only in dated methodology review pending calibration and adoption.

harm_impact_assessment.assessment_gap: The investigation used synthetic teen profiles; it shows no confirmed directly harmed minor or other materialised consequence meeting current HIM 1.0.1 criteria. Clinician referral triggers, notification activation telemetry, population exposure to tested failure pathways and downstream consequences remain unknown or disputed.
